ministry: Ministry of Development of North-East Region
title: MDoNER and CHEMEXCIL Organise Industry Summit on Prospects & Export of Agarwood Oil from India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Development of North-East Region MDoNER and CHEMEXCIL Organise Industry Summit on Prospects & Export of Agarwood Oil from India Roadmap for Agarwood Export Promotion from the North Eastern Region Released North Eastern Region Home to Over 96% of India's Agarwood Resource Base, Offering a Major Export Opportunity Posted On:
                11 AUG 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi An Industry Summit on Prospects & Export of Agarwood Oil from India , organised by the Chemicals and Allied Products Export Promotion Council (CHEMEXCIL) in association with the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER), was held today in New Delhi. The Summit brought together representatives of the fragrance, essential-oil, perfumery, incense, processing and export industries, scientific institutions, policymakers and regulatory agencies on a common platform to deliberate on the commercial prospects and export of Indian agarwood, particularly from the North Eastern Region (NER). Minister of State for Development of North Eastern Region, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Secretary, MDoNER, Shri Katikithala Srinivas, Joint Secretary, MDoNER, Shri Angshuman Dey, Joint Secretary, Ministry of MSME, Ms. Mercy Epao, Chairman, CHEMEXCIL, Shri Satish Wagh and other industry experts and leaders attended the Summit. Resonating with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's perspective of “Yahi Samay Hai, Sahi Samay Hai,” MoS, MDoNER, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar appealed to industry leaders and experts to come forward and invest in the Agarwood sector. He said that industry should come forward, invest, integrate cutting-edge extraction and distillation technology, build world-class brands and form global commercial alliances. Shri Majumdar expressed his gratitude for Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, with emphasis on "Vocal for Local" to "Local to Global." Shri K. Srinivas, Secretary, MDoNER, in his speech, expressed his appreciation for all stakeholders coming together for the joint cause of shaping the future of Indian agarwood and oud oil exports, global market trends, and quality standards. He further stated that the Ministry of DoNER is committed to realizing the potential of the Indian Agarwood Oil industry, its sustainability and global outreach. During the event, Joint Secretary, MDoNER, Shri Angshuman Dey, read out a message from the Hon’ble Minister of DoNER, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, highlighting his vision for the growth of the Agarwood Sector. In his message, Shri Scindia made five specific requests to the industry partners. First, build long-term market linkages with FPOs and cluster-based organizations, giving growers the confidence of assured demand. Second, invest where the resource grows. Greater processing and distillation capacity within the Northeast will ensure that more value and opportunities remain with growers and communities. Third, deepen technology partnerships in advanced extraction, distillation and scientific cultivation to improve quality, yield and global competitiveness. Fourth, build a strong identity for Indian agarwood through standards, certification, traceability and origin branding. enabling producers to command the premium this extraordinary resource deserves. Fifth, invest in the story of Indian oud. Our agarwood carries the heritage, knowledge and livelihoods of the Northeast. The Minister also said that our objective must be clear. The Northeast should not remain merely a supplier of raw material to global luxury markets but become the origin, the standard, the science and the brand of Indian agarwood. He called upon all industry and institutional partners to work shoulder to shoulder towards building a strong, sustainable and globally competitive agarwood ecosystem in the North Eastern Region, creating greater value for growers while taking the fragrance of Indian oud to markets across the world and ensuring “Khushboo Bhi Humari Ho, Aur Naam Bhi Humara.” North Eastern Region is Home to Over 96% of India’s Agarwood Trees - Agarwood is the highly valued resinous aromatic wood of Aquilaria species, primarily processed into agarwood chips and agar oil for perfumery, incense and other premium products. India has an estimated 139.89 million agarwood trees, nearly 96.6% of which are located in the North Eastern Region. Assam alone accounts for about 114.3 million trees, followed by Tripura with about 15.15 million trees, with resources also present in Manipur, Nagaland, Meghalaya and other North Eastern States. Globally, agarwood has strong demand in the Gulf markets, while its use in premium fragrances and other high-value applications is also expanding across Europe, the United States and East Asia. The growing policy focus on the sector is reflected in the recognition accorded to agar tree promotion in the Union Budget 2026-27 and the emphasis on focused export promotion at the 73rd NEC Plenary held in June 2026. Roadmap for Agarwood Export Promotion from NER Released – A key highlight of the Summit was the release of the Roadmap for Agarwood Export Promotion from the North Eastern Region , which provides a focused framework for coordinated action involving relevant Government agencies, North Eastern States, Export Promotion Councils and other stakeholders to facilitate exports, strengthen market linkages and promote regular, compliant and higher-value trade in agarwood and its products. MDoNER has been playing a coordinating and facilitating role in bringing together concerned Central Ministries/Departments, North Eastern State Governments, scientific institutions and export-promotion agencies for development of the agarwood sector in the NER. The Ministry constituted an Inter-Ministerial Task Force in November 2023, whose recommendations were translated into a comprehensive roadmap for promotion of agarwood in the North Eastern Region. Subsequently, an Agarwood Steering Group was constituted in February 2025 to provide a standing mechanism for coordinated action across regulatory facilitation, resource development, technology, and infrastructure and market access. Under the aegis of the approved Roadmap and coordinated action between NE State Governments and technical institutions (ICFRE-RFRI, FFDC, NIPER, NESAC) several key measures have been started which includes enhancement of the agarwood export quota, digitisation of the Certificate of Origin, facilitation for personal carriage of specified agarwood products, resource mapping in Assam and Tripura, empanelment of validated inoculum suppliers, and initiation of GI registration and standard development for agarwood oil. In parallel, MDoNER has supported value addition and market infrastructure through the Agarwood Cluster Development Project in Assam and Tripura under PM-DevINE and the Agarwood International Trade and Research Centre in Agartala under Schemes of NEC. An Agarwood Export Promotion Cell was constituted in May 2026, bringing onboard the concerned Division of the Ministry of Commerce and the nominated Export Promotion Councils - CHEMEXCIL and SHEFEXIL - for focused action on export promotion, exporter facilitation and market development. The Summit and the release of the Export Promotion Roadmap seek to take the sector into its next phase - from coordinated Government facilitation towards sustained industry-led market development for agarwood export promotion from the North Eastern Region. * * * * * * * * PS (Release ID: 2297732) Visitor Counter : 148 Ministry of Development of North-East Region MDoNER and CHEMEXCIL Organise Industry Summit on Prospects & Export of Agarwood Oil from India Roadmap for Agarwood Export Promotion from the North Eastern Region Released North Eastern Region Home to Over 96% of India's Agarwood Resource Base, Offering a Major Export Opportunity Posted On:

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: ALLOCATION FOR FISHERIES SECTOR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying ALLOCATION FOR FISHERIES SECTOR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore, with effect from the financial year 2020-21 for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in all States/UnionTerritories. PMMSY inter-alia provides financial assistance for development of fisheries infrastructure including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, fish markets, cold storages, ice plants, wholesale fish markets, hatcheries, brood banks amongst others. In addition, the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) implemented with effect from the financial year 2018-19 by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides concessional finance to various Eligible Entities including State Governments/Union Territories for development of fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure. The key infrastructure activities approved under these schemes (PMMSY and FIDF) includes; 184 fishing harbours and fish landing centres, 775 cold storages and ice plants,1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets, 28,489 units of fish transportation facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 auto rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks. Despite rising tariff barriers and shifting global trade patterns, India's marine product exports reached 19.72 lakh metric tonnes, valued at Rs. 73,890 crore (USD 8.46 billion) during 2025-26. The share of value-added products in seafood exports increase from 2% in 2013-14 to 11% in 2024-25. The marine exports were made to over 128 countries. The United States remained India's largest export market, followed by China, the European Union (EU), Southeast Asia (SEA), Japan, the Middle East, and other countries. For the sustainable growth of seafood exports, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Commerce and the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) and Export Inspection Council has undertaken various initiatives to diversify export markets. These initiatives includes, sensitization and awareness programmes on the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), conducting stakeholder consultations, organizing Chintan Shivirs on value addition, identifying new export markets and deepening India's presence in existing markets to enhance trade facilitation, promoting exports through trade delegations and international trade fairs, organizing Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs) and Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), National Workshop on Seafood Exports and collaborating with Indian Missions abroad to facilitate market access. The Department of Fisheries has also held a series of Round Table meetings with the Embassies and High Commissions of potential partner countries to explore avenues for collaboration, strengthen bilateral trade cooperation in the fisheries sector. Further, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India is promoting diversified aquaculture under the PMMSY by encouraging the culture of high-value species such as seabass, cobia, pompano, mud crab, GIFT tilapia, grouper, Penaeus monodon, scampi, and seaweed, with a focus on identifying new export markets and deepening existing ones for global competitiveness of Indian seafood. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is also promoting value addition, enhancing biosecurity and quality compliance, encouraging automation and Research and Development (R&D) collaboration, and sustainable fisheries development. In addition, the Government continues to engage with importing countries to address sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) issues, export certification requirements, and market access barriers, while strengthening laboratory infrastructure, residue monitoring, and quality control systems to ensure compliance with international standards. The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying has reported that,100% financial assistance is provided  to States/UTs for prevention of economically important livestock diseases namely Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF) through vaccination. Further, financial assistance is also provided to States/ UTs on sharing basis for State prioritized activities such as vaccination against other livestock diseases, control of emergent and exotic diseases, strengthening of laboratory, disease surveillance, training and awareness. It is reported that 147.05 crore, 3.19 crore, 6.74 crore and 0.26 crore doses of Vaccine for FMD, brucella and PPR and classical swine fever are administered respectively. The total   34.62 crore, doses of Vaccine have been administered for lumpy skin disease. Financial assistance is provided to the 29 States/Union Territories on sharing basis for operation of 4019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVU) to deliver veterinary services at farmer’s doorstep. The livestock disease outbreak has been reduced from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. ***** JP.                         11 AUG 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total outlay of Rs. 20,750 crore, with effect from the financial year 2020-21 for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in all States/UnionTerritories. PMMSY inter-alia provides financial assistance for development of fisheries infrastructure including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, fish markets, cold storages, ice plants, wholesale fish markets, hatcheries, brood banks amongst others. In addition, the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) implemented with effect from the financial year 2018-19 by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides concessional finance to various Eligible Entities including State Governments/Union Territories for development of fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure. The key infrastructure activities approved under these schemes (PMMSY and FIDF) includes; 184 fishing harbours and fish landing centres, 775 cold storages and ice plants,1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets, 28,489 units of fish transportation facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 auto rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks. Despite rising tariff barriers and shifting global trade patterns, India's marine product exports reached 19.72 lakh metric tonnes, valued at Rs. 73,890 crore (USD 8.46 billion) during 2025-26. The share of value-added products in seafood exports increase from 2% in 2013-14 to 11% in 2024-25. The marine exports were made to over 128 countries. The United States remained India's largest export market, followed by China, the European Union (EU), Southeast Asia (SEA), Japan, the Middle East, and other countries. For the sustainable growth of seafood exports, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Commerce and the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) and Export Inspection Council has undertaken various initiatives to diversify export markets. These initiatives includes, sensitization and awareness programmes on the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), conducting stakeholder consultations, organizing Chintan Shivirs on value addition, identifying new export markets and deepening India's presence in existing markets to enhance trade facilitation, promoting exports through trade delegations and international trade fairs, organizing Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs) and Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), National Workshop on Seafood Exports and collaborating with Indian Missions abroad to facilitate market access. The Department of Fisheries has also held a series of Round Table meetings with the Embassies and High Commissions of potential partner countries to explore avenues for collaboration, strengthen bilateral trade cooperation in the fisheries sector. Further, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India is promoting diversified aquaculture under the PMMSY by encouraging the culture of high-value species such as seabass, cobia, pompano, mud crab, GIFT tilapia, grouper, Penaeus monodon, scampi, and seaweed, with a focus on identifying new export markets and deepening existing ones for global competitiveness of Indian seafood. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is also promoting value addition, enhancing biosecurity and quality compliance, encouraging automation and Research and Development (R&D) collaboration, and sustainable fisheries development. In addition, the Government continues to engage with importing countries to address sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) issues, export certification requirements, and market access barriers, while strengthening laboratory infrastructure, residue monitoring, and quality control systems to ensure compliance with international standards. The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying has reported that,100% financial assistance is provided  to States/UTs for prevention of economically important livestock diseases namely Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF) through vaccination. Further, financial assistance is also provided to States/ UTs on sharing basis for State prioritized activities such as vaccination against other livestock diseases, control of emergent and exotic diseases, strengthening of laboratory, disease surveillance, training and awareness. It is reported that 147.05 crore, 3.19 crore, 6.74 crore and 0.26 crore doses of Vaccine for FMD, brucella and PPR and classical swine fever are administered respectively. The total   34.62 crore, doses of Vaccine have been administered for lumpy skin disease. Financial assistance is provided to the 29 States/Union Territories on sharing basis for operation of 4019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVU) to deliver veterinary services at farmer’s doorstep. The livestock disease outbreak has been reduced from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying STATUS OF PM-MKSSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing a Central Sector Sub-scheme namely the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for a period of four years from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 at an estimated outlay of ₹6000 crore. The National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) was launched under PM-MKSSY to meet the following aims and objectives of the sub-scheme: - Gradual formalization of the unorganized fisheries sector including creation of work based digital identities of fish workers for improved service delivery. Facilitating greater access to institutional finance including working capital in order to enable the fish farmers, fishers and micro and small enterprises to reduce their capital cost and to expand their operations. Strengthening fisheries cooperatives by enhancing their institutional capacity, improving market access, facilitating access to finance, and business development plans and need based support. Providing one-time incentive to the fish farmers for purchase of aquaculture insurance. Incentivizing fisheries and aquaculture microenterprises to improve value-chain efficiencies and to create and maintain jobs through performance grants. Incentivizing micro and small enterprises in the fisheries sector to establish supply chains of safe fish and fishery products including creation and maintenance of jobs through performance grants. Under the PM-MKSSY, the Sub-scheme provides support for: (i) formalization of the unorganized part of fisheries sector through National Fisheries Digital Platform and its Apps (ii) facilitating access to institutional credit, (iii) adoption of aquaculture insurance by providing ‘one-time incentive’ to the farmers by providing 40% of the premium (up to ₹25,000 per hectare, or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares, SC/ST and women beneficiaries get an additional 10% incentive (iv) improvement of fisheries value-chain efficiencies and establishment of supply chains of safe fish products to consumers through Performance grant for a Microenterprise i.e. 25% of the total investment or Rs.35 lakhs, whichever is lower, for General Category and 35% of total investment or Rs.45 lakhs, whichever is lower, for SC, ST and Women owned microenterprises. In addition, Performance Grant for Village Level Organizations and Federations of SHGs, FFPOs and Cooperatives shall not exceed 35% of total investment or Rs.200 lakhs, whichever is lower. Along with this, PM-MKSSY aims to provide an amount of Rs.10,000 and Rs.15,000 per year for creation and maintenance of jobs for men and woman respectively subject to the limit of 50% of total eligible grant. As on 06-08-2026, about 35.92 lakh fishers, fish farmers and other stakeholders have registered on NFDP. A total of 3829 primary fisheries cooperatives has been approved for strengthening at a total cost of Rs. 72.75 crores. Aquaculture Insurance policies for 2294 hectare has been covered against which 127 beneficiaries covering 321.74 ha have availed the One-Time Incentive (OTI) amounting to Rs. 40.03 lakh. Further, under the Credit Module, 535 loans have been sanctioned by the banks with loan amount of Rs 28.04 crores and 180 beneficiaries have availed the Success Fee benefit. Under Performance Grant, 84 applications have been approved with eligible Performance Grant of Rs.20.55 crore, out of these, an amount of Rs. 4.33 crore has been released to 21 beneficiaries. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: POST-HARVEST LOSS AND BYCATCH FROM MARINE FISHERIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying POST-HARVEST LOSS AND BYCATCH FROM MARINE FISHERIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) during the year 2023-24 carried out a comprehensive study through the National Productivity Council of India (NPC), an autonomous organization under Ministry of Commerce and Industry to assess post-harvest losses in fisheries and aquaculture sector. The study estimated post-harvest loss in marine fisheries in Karnataka between 6.21% to 10.13%.  Further, Government of Karnataka has also reported that as per the studies done by the ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology(CIFT) the estimated post-harvest loss is around 6%. It is also reported by Government of Karnataka that as per the studies done by the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) the bycatch was reported around 20-40% based on the type of gear and craft used in marine fisheries. The DoF, GoI, under its schemes and policy accords high priory towards strengthening cold chain facilities, reduction of bycatch and efficient utilization of fish harvested. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), implemented by the DoF, GoI envisages support towards creation and modernization of post-harvest and cold chain infrastructure to reduce post-harvest losses, improve value realization, enhance shelf life of fishes harvested. The DoF, GoI encourages adoption of sustainable measures to minimize marine bycatch. Concurrently, States/Union Territories (UTs) are also encouraged towards optimal and value-added utilization of all harvested resources, thereby reducing post-harvest losses and promoting a circular economy in the fisheries sector. During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026-27) under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has accorded approval to the fisheries development proposals of Government of Karnataka with a total project cost amounting to ₹ 1053.60 crore. The approved activities inter-alia also included cold chain facilities like establishment of Ice plants/cold storages (126 units.), post-harvest transportation units (1065 units) which included refrigerated vehicles, insulated vehicles, motor cycle with ice boxes, cycle with ice boxes, three wheelers with ice boxes etc.,  live fish vending centres (46 units), fish kiosks (100 units), fish retail market (1 unit), matsya vahini mobile eco-friendly fish kiosks (300 units) and state of art whole sale fish market (1 unit). Under PMMSY, identification and selection of beneficiaries are carried out by the respective State Governments. The Government of Karnataka has informed that 171 beneficiaries have been supported under the cold chain infrastructure component of PMMSY. Under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has approved modernization and upgradation of Mangaluru Fishing Harbour at project cost of ₹ 37.47 crore which envisages improved berthing facilities, modern fish landing and auction infrastructure, hygienic fish handling areas, upgraded water supply, sanitation and waste management facilities, and upgraded harbour utilities to minimize handling losses and improve fish quality. In addition, in the adjoining areas projects namely modernization of Gangolli Fishing Harbour (₹ 22.18 crore) and Malpe Fishing Harbour (₹ 12.52 crore) has also been approved for providing similar facilities. Government of Karnataka has also informed that fishermen are encouraged to use Square-mesh cod-end trawl nets (35 mm) to allow juveniles to escape, and to install Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets to allow turtles to escape; both measures aimed towards conservation and sustainable fisheries. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. ***** JP. title: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMMSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMMSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi Indian Council of Agricultural Research – Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute ( ICAR‑CMFRI) undertakes continuous monitoring of fish landings, conducts focused biological research, and tracks coastal ecosystem health through real‑time surveys across coastal States/UTs, including in Andhra Pradesh. The Fishery Survey of India (FSI) similarly conducts systematic exploratory surveys in the EEZ, generating baseline data on demersal and oceanic stocks to support assessments of impacts from fishing pressure, climate variability, pollution, and habitat degradation. Available scientific evidence from these institutions indicates that while environmental stressors affect the distribution, abundance, and seasonal availability of certain species, no direct and conclusive impact on overall marine fish production has been established solely due to climate variability and marine pollution. Further, as per the Marine Fish Stock Status of India (2022) of ICAR‑CMFRI, 91.1% of the 135 assessed marine fish stocks in the Indian EEZ are at sustainable levels. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) across all States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, since 2020–21. Under PMMSY, proposals amounting to ₹21,461.03 crore, with a Central share of ₹9,571.09 crore, have been approved for all States/UTs. For Andhra Pradesh, proposals of ₹2,328.89 crore, including a Central share of ₹681.38 crore, have been sanctioned. PMMSY also supports long‑term resource enhancement measures such as installation of Artificial Reefs and Sea Ranching to improve fish availability and strengthen fishers’ livelihoods. Under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), 253 projects have been approved at a total cost of ₹6,657.57 crore, with ₹4,979.04 crore considered for interest subvention, for various States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh. The Department implements the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) under PMMSY through the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB). During 2021‑22 to 2026‑27, the Central Government released ₹130.68 crore to provide insurance coverage to 167.64 lakh fishers, averaging 33.52 lakh fishers per year. State‑wise details of fishers insured and claims settled are at Annexure‑I . Additionally, the Government of Andhra Pradesh has reported provision of ₹150.00 crore as diesel subsidy to 63,840 beneficiaries during 2023‑24 to 2025‑26. Further, ₹511.46 crore has been provided to 2,55,731 marine fishers during the fishing ban period in 2025‑26 and 2026‑27. Under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides livelihood and nutritional support to socio‑economically backward active traditional fishers’ families during the fishing ban and lean season, with the objective of conserving fish resources. Further, to augment fish stocks in coastal waters, the Department is working closely with State Governments on a range of resource‑enhancement measures, including establishment of artificial reefs along the coastline, conduct of sea ranching, and implementation of a uniform, annual fishing closure during the critical fish breeding period. *** Annexure- I STATEMEN T REGARDING FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMMSY: Sl No. Name Of States No of Fishers Insured Claims Settled Amount Settled (i) (ii) (iii) (vii) (viii) 1 Arunachal Pradesh 4,173 0 0 2 Assam 8,83,630 4 15,23,746 3 Bihar 7,50,000 3 15,00,000 4 Chhattisgarh 11,02,377 12 57,50,000 5 Goa 14,540 1 5,00,000 6 Gujarat 4,91,237 10 50,00,000 7 Haryana 8,076 0 0 8 Himachal Pradesh 54,988 6 25,75,000 9 Jharkhand 8,36,991 4 20,00,000 10 Karnataka 3,62,371 21 1,05,00,000 11 Madhya Pradesh 5,04,264 1 5,00,000 12 Maharashtra 5,25,519 25 1,25,00,000 13 Manipur 8,534 1 5,00,000 14 Meghalaya 4,280 0 0 15 Odisha 53,91,593 102 4,70,14,059 16 Punjab 15,959 0 0 17 Rajasthan 24,426 2 10,00,000 18 Sikkim 2,905 0 0 19 Tamil Nadu 27,81,317 591 28,13,16,727 20 Telangana 18,53,832 948 47,03,89,005 21 Tripura 1,81,724 0 0 22 Uttar Pradesh 5,19,570 5 20,21,385 23 Uttarakhand 18,115 0 0 24 West Bengal 8,499 0 0 TOTAL 1,63,48,920 1,736 84,45,89,922 UNION TERRITORIES 1 Andaman & Nicobar 65,087 3 15,00,000 2 Delhi 1,881 0 0 3 Daman & Diu 38,267 0 0 4 Jammu & Kashmir 1,25,309 5 25,00,000 5 Lakshadweep 11,142 2 5,18,224 6 Ladakh 2,674 0 0 7 Puducherry 1,71,456 28 1,25,75,000 TOTAL 4,15,816 38 1,70,93,224 Grand Total 1,67,64,736 1,774 86,16,83,146 This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. **** JP. PMMSY also supports long‑term resource enhancement measures such as installation of Artificial Reefs and Sea Ranching to improve fish availability and strengthen fishers’ livelihoods. Under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), 253 projects have been approved at a total cost of ₹6,657.57 crore, with ₹4,979.04 crore considered for interest subvention, for various States/UTs including Andhra Pradesh. The Department implements the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) under PMMSY through the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB). During 2021‑22 to 2026‑27, the Central Government released ₹130.68 crore to provide insurance coverage to 167.64 lakh fishers, averaging 33.52 lakh fishers per year. State‑wise details of fishers insured and claims settled are at Annexure‑I . Additionally, the Government of Andhra Pradesh has reported provision of ₹150.00 crore as diesel subsidy to 63,840 beneficiaries during 2023‑24 to 2025‑26. Further, ₹511.46 crore has been provided to 2,55,731 marine fishers during the fishing ban period in 2025‑26 and 2026‑27. Under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides livelihood and nutritional support to socio‑economically backward active traditional fishers’ families during the fishing ban and lean season, with the objective of conserving fish resources. Further, to augment fish stocks in coastal waters, the Department is working closely with State Governments on a range of resource‑enhancement measures, including establishment of artificial reefs along the coastline, conduct of sea ranching, and implementation of a uniform, annual fishing closure during the critical fish breeding period. *** Annexure- I STATEMEN T REGARDING FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMMSY: Sl No. Name Of States No of Fishers Insured Claims Settled Amount Settled (i) (ii) (iii) (vii) (viii) 1 Arunachal Pradesh 4,173 0 0 2 Assam 8,83,630 4 15,23,746 3 Bihar 7,50,000 3 15,00,000 4 Chhattisgarh 11,02,377 12 57,50,000 5 Goa 14,540 1 5,00,000 6 Gujarat 4,91,237 10 50,00,000 7 Haryana 8,076 0 0 8 Himachal Pradesh 54,988 6 25,75,000 9 Jharkhand 8,36,991 4 20,00,000 10 Karnataka 3,62,371 21 1,05,00,000 11 Madhya Pradesh 5,04,264 1 5,00,000 12 Maharashtra 5,25,519 25 1,25,00,000 13 Manipur 8,534 1 5,00,000 14 Meghalaya 4,280 0 0 15 Odisha 53,91,593 102 4,70,14,059 16 Punjab 15,959 0 0 17 Rajasthan 24,426 2 10,00,000 18 Sikkim 2,905 0 0 19 Tamil Nadu 27,81,317 591 28,13,16,727 20 Telangana 18,53,832 948 47,03,89,005 21 Tripura 1,81,724 0 0 22 Uttar Pradesh 5,19,570 5 20,21,385 23 Uttarakhand 18,115 0 0 24 West Bengal 8,499 0 0 TOTAL 1,63,48,920 1,736 84,45,89,922 UNION TERRITORIES 1 Andaman & Nicobar 65,087 3 15,00,000 2 Delhi 1,881 0 0 3 Daman & Diu 38,267 0 0 4 Jammu & Kashmir 1,25,309 5 25,00,000 5 Lakshadweep 11,142 2 5,18,224 6 Ladakh 2,674 0 0 7 Puducherry 1,71,456 28 1,25,75,000 TOTAL 4,15,816 38 1,70,93,224 Grand Total 1,67,64,736 1,774 86,16,83,146 This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. **** JP. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: PROMOTION OF INLAND FISHERIES EXPORT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying PROMOTION OF INLAND FISHERIES EXPORT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi To promote sustainable seafood exports from Inland States and Union Territories, the Department of Fisheries, in consultation with the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), Export Inspection Council (EIC) and National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), has prepared a draft guidance document for promoting the participation of Inland States and Union Territories in India's seafood export value chain. The guidance document provides a roadmap for strengthening export readiness by promoting quality assurance, traceability, institutional coordination, post-harvest management, value addition, market access and capacity building. Further, the Department, in collaboration with MPEDA and NFDB, is undertaking awareness programmes, exposure visits and capacity-building initiatives to promote export-oriented inland aquaculture and facilitate greater participation of inland States and Union Territories in seafood exports. (b) The Government has undertaken several measures to strengthen the inland fisheries export value chain. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), priority has been accorded to post‑harvest handling, cold chain development, fish processing, logistics and marketing. The Department of Fisheries has approved the proposals amounting to ₹2,797 crore for development of cold chain and marketing infrastructure across the country. The approved projects include 775 cold storages and ice plants, 28,489 fish transportation units, 1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets and 24 wholesale fish markets, thereby improving post-harvest management, cold chain, transportation and market connectivity. To support quality certification and compliance with international standards, the EIC conducts inspection, certification and capacity-building programmes for seafood exporters. The MPEDA promotes market access through Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs), Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), participation in international seafood trade fairs and collaboration with Indian Missions abroad. (c) The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, is promoting the adoption of emerging technologies and innovative logistics solutions to improve the transportation of high-value fish and fishery products from production centres to processing and export hubs. To facilitate this, the ICAR-Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CIFRI), in collaboration with the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), is implementing a pilot project to assess the feasibility of using drone technology for transportation of live fish over short distances. The pilot project has been approved at a total cost of ₹116.85 lakh and aims to develop and evaluate a drone system capable of transporting up to 100 kg of live fish over a distance of approximately 10 km, while maintaining fish health and quality and reducing transportation time compared to conventional methods. As part of the project, ICAR-CIFRI has successfully demonstrated transportation of a 70 kg payload over a distance of 7 km, marking significant progress towards the project objective. The project also includes scientific studies on fish behaviour and stress during drone transportation of live fishes, with the objective of ensuring safe and efficient transport through specialised containers designed to regulate water quality, dissolved oxygen and temperature. Further, the Department has constituted a Technical Committee to prepare Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the safe and effective adoption of drone technology in the fisheries sector. (d) PMMSY inter alia lays special focus on training, skill development, skill upgradation and capacity building through trainings, awareness programmes and exposure visits to various stakeholders especially fishers, fish farmers, fish workers, fish vendors, entrepreneurs, officials, fisheries Cooperatives and members of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) for various fishing technology, aquaculture and post-harvest related activities enabling greater participation of these stakeholders in export markets. In addition, the Department of Fisheries signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) with an objective to provide a digital marketplace and empower all stakeholders , including traditional fishermen, fish farmers producer organization, and entrepreneurs from the fisheries sector to buy and sell their products through the e-marketplace for better prices and profitability.  Further, PMMSY has supported 2195 fisheries cooperatives as Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) with a project outlay of Rs. 544.85 crore through the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) and National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) as implementing agencies. (e) The Government of India, through the Department of Commerce, is leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and other bilateral trade engagements to enhance market access for Indian seafood products, including inland fisheries products. The Department of Fisheries, in coordination with the Department of Commerce, MPEDA , and EIC, facilitates compliance with importing countries' requirements, market diversification, and export promotion through participation in international trade fairs, expos, Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs), Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), and trade delegations. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. ******* JP. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: WELFARE SCHEMES FOR FISHERMEN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying WELFARE SCHEMES FOR FISHERMEN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) has been implementing various schemes for the holistic development of the fisheries, welfare and livelihood of fishers in all States/UTs, including Kerala. The major schemes include the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) (2020-21 to 2026-27), the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) (2018-19 to 2025-26), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) (2023-24 to 2026-27), and extension of the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fisheries (since 2018-19). Under PM-MKSSY, the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) was launched to facilitate formalisation of the fisheries and aquaculture sector through creation of a work-based digital identity and database for stakeholders. During the last five years and the current financial year (2026-27), under PMMSY, the DoF, GoI has approved fisheries development proposals of the Government of Kerala amounting to Rs.1,413.91 crore with a central share of Rs. 598.58 crore. Against this, the Central assistance of Rs.462.22 crore has been released. The Government of Kerala has reported that the expenditure of Rs.451.807 crore was utilised towards this release. Under PMMSY, the beneficiary selection is done by the respective State Governments/Union Territories. Government of Kerala has informed that activities like livelihood support during fish ban period, boats & nets for traditional fishermen, Biofloc fish farming, Re-Circulatory Aquaculture System (RAS), backyard ornamental units, brackish water cage, fish kiosk, three wheeler with ice box, motor cycle with ice box and Sagar Mitras are implemented in Vadakara, Kerala. Government of Kerala has also informed that 3 primary societies of Vadakara are selected for Fish Farmers Producer Organisations (FFPOs) under PMMSY. It is further informed that about 7561 beneficiaries are benefitted from Vadakara, Kerala. Under the FIDF, the DoF, GoI has approved 13 projects in Kerala with a total project cost of Rs.551.72 crore. The approval also include an Integrated Fisheries Development Project of MATSYAFED at a total project cost of Rs.35.97 crore, implemented across the State, including Kozhikode district, to provide financial assistance to fishermen for procurement of outboard motors, fishing nets and allied fishing accessories, thereby contributing to improvement in the livelihood and socio-economic well-being of fishermen. No specific proposal to the Vadakara has been received under FIDF. Under PM-MKSSY, as on date, about 35.92 lakh fishers, fish farmers and other stakeholders have registered on NFDP portal including 2,52,301 from Kerala, of whom 5,032 belong to the Vadakara. The DoF, GoI through National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) and Government of Kerala, organized outreach programmes at Ponnani, Malappuram, covering fishers from the Vadakara, to create awareness about schemes of Government of India. DoF GoI has not received any proposal from Government of Kerala towards fisheries infrastructure, fishing harbours, fish landing centres in Vadakara. DoF, GoI accords high priority towards livelihood strengthening, ensuring safety and social security of traditional fishermen in all States/UTs including Kerala. The schemes and policies implemented by the DoF, GoI are strategically aligned to achieve holistic development of the fisheries sector while placing the socio-economic well-being of the fishers at its core. Under the PMMSY the DoF, GoI has approved various fisheries developmental activities to Kerala including interventions towards livelihood and fishers welfare namely, livelihood support for during the fishing ban period (1,71,033 Nos),  support for boats and fishing nets (200 units), establishment of Integrated Modern Coastal Fishing Villages (9 Nos), establishment of Climate Resilient Coastal Fishing Villages (6 Nos), procurement of  deep-sea fishing vessels (20 units), bivalve cultivation (1140 units) as additional employment, fish transportation units (468 units), installation of artificial reefs (42 units) for resource enhancement, establishment of Matsya Seva Kendras (10 Nos) and engagement of Sagar Mitras (222 Nos) for extension and advisory services. Additionally, 18908 Nos of KCC cards have been sanctioned to fisheries beneficiaries in Kerala. All these initiatives are aimed at strengthening of fishers livelihood and safety of fishers in Kerala including Vadakara. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. ***** JP. title: ASSISTANCE TO COASTAL FISHERMEN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying ASSISTANCE TO COASTAL FISHERMEN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi The annual fish production in the country has registered a steady increase from 147.25 lakh tonnes in 2020–21 to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024–25. The year-wise fish production during the period from 2020–21 to 2024–25 is as follows: Sl No Year Fish production (in lakh tonnes) 1 2020-21 147.25 2 2021-22 162.48 3 2022-23 175.45 4 2023-24 183.93 5 2024-25 197.75 The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing the following schemes/ programmes for holistic development of fisheries including welfare of coastal fishermen in the country. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY): The Department has been implementing PMMSY from Financial Year 2020-21 with an estimated investment of Rs.20,750 crore for holistic development of fisheries sector including welfare of fishers and fish farmers in the country. Fisheries & Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF): In order to address the infrastructure requirement for fisheries sector, FIDF was launched in the year 2018-19 with a total funds size of Rs 7522.48 crore. FIDF provides concessional finance to the Eligible Entities (EEs), including State Governments/Union Territories for development of identified fisheries infrastructure facilities. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India provides interest subvention up to 3% per annum for the repayment period of 12 years inclusive of moratorium of 2 years for providing the concessional finance by the Nodal Loaning Entities (NLEs) at the interest rate not lower than 5% per annum. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY): To make the fisheries sector resilient and incentivize adoption of efficiencies in fisheries value chain, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has been implementing a Central Sector Sub-scheme "Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY)" a sub-scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with an investment of Rs. 6000 crore. PMMKSSY aims at formalization of the fisheries sector, incentivizing the aquaculture insurance, fisheries micro and small enterprises value chain efficiency, adoption of safety and quality system for safe fish production etc. Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish farmers: Additionally, the Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018-19 has extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them to meet their working capital requirements. The development of fishing harbours, fish landing centres and fisheries infrastructure facilities is one of the important areas envisaged and are supported under the PMMSY and FIDF. Under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years has approved 28 Fishing Harbour development/ modernization projects, 25 Fish Landing Centre projects, and 23 dredging projects at a total approved cost of Rs. 3,741.89 crore. Under FIDF, t he Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years has approved another 94 fishing harbours and fish landing centres at a total of cost of Rs.4916.46 crore and its projects cost restricted for interest subvention at Rs.3651.19 crore. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India under PMMSY and FIDF has also approved proposals amounting to Rs 2,797 crore for development of cold chain and marketing facilities in the country including coastal areas. The key activities approved includes; 775 cold storages and ice plants, 28,489 units of fish transportation facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 auto rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks, 1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets in all the States and Union Territories. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Highlights Massive Growth in India's Livestock Sector
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Highlights Massive Growth in India's Livestock Sector Over 50 Lakh Farmers Credit-Linked Under KCC; 6.4 Lakh Participate in Digital Training Accelerating Scientific Breeding and Fodder Development Nationally Strengthening Doorstep Veterinary Healthcare and Disease Control प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, announced major developments in India's livestock sector, detailing expanding institutional credit, digital outreach, and livestock productivity. Credit accessibility for animal husbandry farmers reached a key milestone, with Kisan Credit Card (KCC) coverage scaling to 50.42 lakh beneficiaries in FY 2025–26, up from 15.08 lakh in 2021–22. India's annual milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024–25, comfortably surpassing domestic demand (243 million tonnes). Total dairy exports reached $407.18 million in FY 2025–26. To boost long-term yield and genetic resilience, the Ministry is actively expanding flagship schemes across States: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM): To supplement the efforts of the States and UTs in promoting scientific breeding, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India(GoI) is implementing Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) since December 2014 for development and conservation of indigenous breeds, genetic upgradation of bovine population and enhancement of milk production and productivity thereby making milk production more remunerative to farmers. National Livestock Mission (NLM): In order to promote scientific breeding and improve fodder quality in the country, the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India is implementing the scheme of National Livestock Mission since the financial year 2014-15. The scheme of National Livestock Mission (NLM) aims towards employment generation, entrepreneurship development, increase in per animal productivity and thus targeting increased production of meat, goat milk, egg and wool under the umbrella scheme Development Programme. The concept of NLM Scheme is to develop the entrepreneur in order to create the forward and backward linkage for the produce available at the unorganized sector and to link with the organized sector. The major initiatives undertaken by, Government of India (GOI) under the National Livestock Mission (NLM) and Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) to promote livestock development and strengthen animal healthcare services in Tamil Nadu during the last five years are as below:- 50% capital subsidyprovided under NLM-EDP to individuals, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Farmer Cooperative Organisations (FCOs), and Section 8 companies. The NLM scheme focuses on Breed Development of Livestock & Poultry, Feed and Fodder development, Research & Development, Livestock Insurance and Extension. 100% financial assistance is provided under LHDCP to all the States/UTs for prevention of economically important livestock diseases namely Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF) through vaccination. Further, financial assistance is provided to States/ UTs on sharing basis for State prioritised activities such asvaccination against other livestock diseases, control of emergent and exotic diseases, strengthening of laboratory, disease surveillance, training and awareness. Financial assistance is provided to the State of Tamil Nadu on sharing basis for operation of 245 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVU)to deliver veterinary services at farmer’s doorstep. *** SM/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297628) आगंतुक पटल  : 182 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Highlights Massive Growth in India's Livestock Sector Over 50 Lakh Farmers Credit-Linked Under KCC; 6.4 Lakh Participate in Digital Training Accelerating Scientific Breeding and Fodder Development Nationally Strengthening Doorstep Veterinary Healthcare and Disease Control प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: DHR-ICMR’s SHINE 2026 brings school students face-to-face with health research across 83 locations
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare DHR-ICMR’s SHINE 2026 brings school students face-to-face with health research across 83 locations Around 30,000 students to experience health research first-hand Two-day programme being held on 11–12 August across 83 ICMR locations From Keylong to Kerala and Diu to Nagaland, SHINE 2026 takes science across India Students to explore laboratories, witness live demonstrations and interact with ICMR scientists Dr Rajiv Bahl encourages students to stay curious, ask questions and explore science as a career SHINE website launched; nationwide student research competition announced Initiative aims to nurture scientific temper and inspire the next generation of health researchers प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 1:55PM by PIB Delhi The second edition of ICMR-SHINE (Science and Health Innovation for NextGen Explorers) commenced today, as the Department of Health Research (DHR) and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) welcomed school students into their laboratories for a nationwide open-day experience. Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's call for students to “spend one day as a scientist,” the two-day programme is being observed on 11–12 August 2026 across 83 locations nationwide, including ICMR institutes, Model Rural Health Research Units (MRHRUs), and affiliated field units. From Keylong in Himachal Pradesh, at an altitude of nearly 10,000 feet, to Kerala in the south, and from Diu in the west to Nagaland in the east, the program will reach children across the country, bringing them closer to science and encouraging curiosity and interest in scientific enquiry. Speaking on the occasion, Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, DHR & Director General, ICMR, said, “To all the young students joining us today, I encourage you to be curious, ask questions and never be afraid to wonder why. Every discovery begins with a question, and every innovation begins with the courage to explore a new possibility. I hope your experience at SHINE gives you a glimpse of the exciting world of health research and inspires you to consider science not only as something you study, but as a career through which you can make a meaningful difference to people’s lives.” During his interaction with the participating students, Dr Rajiv Bahl engaged with their questions on science, health and research, responding through relatable examples and encouraging them to remain curious and think beyond textbooks. He also inaugurated the exhibition showcasing ICMR’s research work and innovations, giving students an opportunity to explore how scientific discoveries translate into solutions for real-world health challenges. Over these two days, students of Grades 9 to 12 from government and private schools are stepping directly into the world of health research. Participating students are taking part in guided laboratory tours, research exhibitions, poster walks, video presentations, and live demonstrations of ongoing scientific work, and are interacting with ICMR scientists to gain insight into their research journeys, areas of expertise, and everyday work in public health. Bringing the spirit of scientific curiosity to life for the young participants is Dr Curio, the official mascot of SHINE, who features across the initiative's outreach material, posters, and social media, and as the narrator of a series of interactive videos on ICMR's work. To mark the occasion, ICMR also launched the official SHINE website (shine.icmr.org.in), a dedicated platform hosting resources, updates, and opportunities for students interested in health research. Alongside the launch, ICMR announced a nationwide school competition inviting students to frame their own research questions and propose potential solutions to real-world public health challenges. Around 30,000 students are expected to take part in this next phase of the initiative through invitations extended by ICMR laboratories across the country. By opening the doors of its institutes and research units, the program seeks to make science tangible and accessible, showing young learners how research addresses the health challenges facing communities and encouraging them to see a future for themselves in scientific enquiry. Aligned with India's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the initiative reaffirms ICMR's commitment to nurturing scientific temper among the country's youth and to inspiring the next generation of researchers who will contribute to India's health and development goals. *** GS/SR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297527) आगंतुक पटल  : 350 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Kannada , Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Bengali-TR , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Health and Family Welfare DHR-ICMR’s SHINE 2026 brings school students face-to-face with health research across 83 locations Around 30,000 students to experience health research first-hand Two-day programme being held on 11–12 August across 83 ICMR locations From Keylong to Kerala and Diu to Nagaland, SHINE 2026 takes science across India Students to explore laboratories, witness live demonstrations and interact with ICMR scientists Dr Rajiv Bahl encourages students to stay curious, ask questions and explore science as a career SHINE website launched; nationwide student research competition announced Initiative aims to nurture scientific temper and inspire the next generation of health researchers प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Implementation of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational Guidelines
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Implementation of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational Guidelines Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Unveils 7X7X7 Framework to Accelerate Anemia Reduction New Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Guidelines Focus on Testing, Treatment, Tracking and Dietary Diversification प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 1:36PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has recently released the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational guidelines during the 16 th Central Council of Health and Family Welfare (CCHFW) meeting on 29 th June 2026 to address anemia through a 7X7X7 strategy, moving ahead from the older 6X6X6 strategy of Anemia Mukt Bharat programme. The components of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan are: Saturation of Hb testing using Digital Invasive Hemoglobinometers at platforms based on beneficiary group. P rophylaxis and targeted therapeutic management as per category of anemia diagnosed. Segregation of nutritional anemia and non-nutritional anemia for appropriate case-base management. Robust digital system for tracking anemia services: Shift from T3 approach (Test, Treat, Talk) toward T4 approach (Test, Treat, Talk and Track) Dietary diversification with Eat Right Approach and promotion of locally available iron rich foods on everyday basis. Implementation of convergent approach- ‘whole of Government Approach’ for implementation of complementary interventions, inter-ministerial convergence ‘Jan Bhagidari- Communication strategy for transformation of mindset from passive acceptance of anemia to active ownership (for Test, Treat, Talk and Track) The details of 7X7X7 framework under Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan are as follows: The seven beneficiaries are: Children 6-59 months Children 5-9 years Adolescents 10-19 years Pregnant women Lactating mothers Women in reproductive age (20-49 years) 0-6 months LBW babies The seven interventions are: Prophylactic IFA Supplementation Testing of anemia Therapeutic management of anemia Deworming and Delayed Cord Clamping Jan Bhagidari- communication strategy to counteract normalised perception of anemia and improve compliance to IFA supplementation Addressing non-nutritional causes of anemia Eating Right – promotion of locally available iron rich food and diet diversification The seven Institutional mechanisms are: Intra-ministerial coordination National Centre of Excellence and Advanced Research on Anemia National AMB Abhiyaan Unit Strengthening supply chain and logistics Convergence with other Ministries Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Portal Digital Framework for monitoring through T4 approach The T4 approach includes Testing for anemia, Treatment for anemia, Talk for awareness and compliance through Jan Bhagidari, and Tracking the beneficiaries for treatment, referral and follow-up. The digital framework has been entailed under Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to record, strengthen digital tracking and monitoring of anemia services. The beneficiaries are tested for anemia across platforms, pregnant and lactating mothers registered in JANANI Portal, school going children registered in RBSK portal and children for vaccination registered in U-WIN portal. The categorization of anemia into mild, moderate and severe anemia and appropriate management of anemia as per protocols is envisioned under Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** SR HFW/PQ-Implementation of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan/11 August 2026/1 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297512) आगंतुक पटल  : 322 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Telugu Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Implementation of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational Guidelines Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Unveils 7X7X7 Framework to Accelerate Anemia Reduction New Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Guidelines Focus on Testing, Treatment, Tracking and Dietary Diversification प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Steps Taken to Promote Menstrual Health and Hygiene
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken to Promote Menstrual Health and Hygiene Under the National Health Mission, States/UTs are supported for Menstrual Hygiene Schemes based on their proposals in their Annual Programme Implementation Plans Union Health Ministry implements the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme for promotion of menstrual hygiene among adolescent girls Monitoring under NHM is carried out through a robust, multi-layered framework that includes review of State-wise Key Deliverables against approved targets during NPCC meetings with all States/UT Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-going Girls is implemented through coordinated action by States/UTs to promote access to safe, effective and affordable menstrual hygiene measures in schools प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi Menstrual Health and Hygiene Management (MHM) is a multidimensional and inter-ministerial issue requiring coordinated action by multiple stakeholder Ministries/Departments and States/Union Territories in accordance with their respective statutory mandates. Under the National Health Mission (NHM), States/UTs are supported for Menstrual Hygiene Schemes based on their proposals in their Annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) as per the regulatory norms. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare implements the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme (MHS) for promotion of menstrual hygiene among adolescent girls. The Scheme focuses on awareness generation, access to quality and affordable sanitary napkins, safe and environment-friendly disposal, and counselling on safe menstrual practices. In furtherance of its public health mandate, the Ministry undertakes sustained Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities, awareness generation and sensitization programmes through health facilities, community platforms, frontline health workers, digital dissemination mechanisms and adolescent-focused programme platforms. Monitoring under the National Health Mission (NHM) is carried out through a robust, multi-layered framework that includes review of State-wise Key Deliverables against approved targets during NPCC meetings with all States/UTs. In addition, annual Common Review Missions (CRMs) provide independent, on-ground assessments of programme implementation, health system strengthening, and progress on key indicators. In collaboration with concerned line Ministries, the Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-going Girls is implemented through coordinated action by States/UTs to promote access to safe, effective and affordable menstrual hygiene measures in schools through their respective and concerned departments. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. title: Steps taken for Promotion and Regulation of Regenerative Medicines
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken for Promotion and Regulation of Regenerative Medicines Union Health Ministry has Issued Comprehensive Guidelines to Promote Safe and Evidence-Based Use of Regenerative Medicines Department of Biotechnology supports fundamental and translational research towards development of indigenous regenerative medicine technologies involving stem cell/in-vitro systems for various diseases including hematological and genetic disorders Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council - Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine, an autonomous institute under DBT has contributed to the advancement of translational regenerative medicine in India through innovations Department of Health Research has established mechanism to facilitate and promote biomedical research and conduct of clinical trials in the country through ethics committees registered with DHR ICMR promotes indigenous research and innovation in regenerative medicine through support for basic, preclinical and clinical research, development of indigenous technologies, and generation of scientific evidence through various funding programmes प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi The following guidelines on regenerative medicines have been issued and are available in public domain- i. Centre for Evidence Based Guidelines, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has issued ‘Evidence based guidelines for the use of stem cell therapy’ in 2025-2026 regarding the efficacy and safety of stem cell therapy in various disease indications. These recommendations were formulated after careful consideration of the available evidence based on the methodology as described by international agencies like the World Health Organization (WHO) and National institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) in UK. These Guidelines can be accessed online at:- https://www.dhr.gov.in/offerings/schemes-and-services/details/centre-for-evidence-based-guidelines-EzN1MTMtQWa ii. Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has informed that it issued a document in 2023 on ‘ Guidelines for Umbilical Cord Blood Banking Collection, Processing, Testing, Storage, Banking and Release for Clinical Application’. It can be accessed online at: https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/custom_data/pdf/resource-guidelines/GUCBB_F.pdf iii. ICMR has issued “ National Guidelines for Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (NGHCT)” in 2021. This document can be accessed online at:- https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/custom_data/pdf/resource-guidelines/Nat_Guide_HCT.pdf iv. ICMR in collaboration with Department of Biotechnology (DBT) has issued “National Guidelines for Gene Therapy Product Development and Clinical Trials” in 2019 to guide and enable the stakeholders to comprehend and comply with the regulatory requirements for research and development of Gene Therapy Products in India. These can be accessed online at:- https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/custom_data/pdf/resource-guidelines/guidelines_GTP.pdf v. ICMR along with DBT has also issued ‘National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research (NGSCR-2017)’. This document provides guidance to all stakeholders including scientists, clinicians and industry and can be accessed online ( https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/custom_data/pdf/resource-guidelines/Guidelines_for_stem_cell_research_2017.pdf ). Further, DBT has informed that it supports fundamental and translational research towards development of indigenous regenerative medicine technologies involving stem cell/in-vitro systems for various diseases including hematological and genetic disorders. Department’s autonomous institute, Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council – Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (BRIC-inStem) has also contributed to the advancement of translational regenerative medicine in India through innovations. For example, country's first-in-human gene therapy clinical trial was conducted by the Centre for Stem Cell Research (CSCR), Vellore, a unit of BRIC-inStem, in collaboration with Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore. The Department of Health Research (DHR) has established mechanism to facilitate and promote biomedical research and conduct of clinical trials in the country through ethics committees registered with DHR. The National Stem Cell Research Regulation Committee (NSRC) provides oversight of clinical stem cell research involving minimally manipulated stem cells.  All proposals approved by an Institutional Ethics Committee for such research must be forwarded to NSRC before the research commences. Clinical trials and manufacture of regenerative medicine products that fall within the ambit of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 continue to be regulated by Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO). ICMR promotes indigenous research and innovation in regenerative medicine through support for basic, preclinical and clinical research, development of indigenous technologies, and generation of scientific evidence through various funding programmes. DBT has informed that it also nurtures and caters support to develop solutions using cell and gene-based therapies to reduce the high developmental cost burden through its multidisciplinary research and advanced research programmes. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. **** SR HFW/PQ-Steps taken for Promotion and Regulation of Regenerative Medicines/11 August 2026/4 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297509) आगंतुक पटल  : 153 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken for Promotion and Regulation of Regenerative Medicines Union Health Ministry has Issued Comprehensive Guidelines to Promote Safe and Evidence-Based Use of Regenerative Medicines Department of Biotechnology supports fundamental and translational research towards development of indigenous regenerative medicine technologies involving stem cell/in-vitro systems for various diseases including hematological and genetic disorders Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council - Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine, an autonomous institute under DBT has contributed to the advancement of translational regenerative medicine in India through innovations Department of Health Research has established mechanism to facilitate and promote biomedical research and conduct of clinical trials in the country through ethics committees registered with DHR ICMR promotes indigenous research and innovation in regenerative medicine through support for basic, preclinical and clinical research, development of indigenous technologies, and generation of scientific evidence through various funding programmes प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Update on Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme PMNDP is presently implemented in all 36 States/UTs covering 751 districts, including 44 linked districts through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines Union Health Ministry undertakes regular review of the Programme; non-operational dialysis centres, if any, are brought to the notice of the concerned State/UT for taking corrective action प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi ‘Public Health’ and ‘Hospitals’ are state subjects. However, the Government of India provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs under the National Health Mission (NHM) for strengthening healthcare infrastructure, including dialysis services. Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP) was launched to improve access to haemodialysis services by establishing dialysis centres in District Hospitals and other health facilities across the country and providing free dialysis services to eligible patients. The Programme is presently implemented in all 36 States/UTs covering 751 districts (including 44 linked districts) through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines, as reported by the States/UTs as on 30.06.2026. Dialysis centres under PMNDP were established based on proposals received from the States/UTs in their annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs), prepared on the basis of gap analysis. These proposals are considered in the National Programme Coordination Committee meetings and approvals are conveyed through the Record of Proceedings (RoPs). The State/UT-wise cumulative number of dialysis centres established under PMNDP, including those added during the last two years, is at Annexure-I. The Ministry undertakes periodic monitoring of the Programme through the Common Review Mission (CRM) and visits by senior officers. During such reviews, non-operational dialysis centres, if any, are brought to the notice of the concerned State/UT for taking corrective action. The responsibility for timely operationalization of dialysis centres, deployment of adequately trained manpower including dialysis technicians, rests with the respective State/UT Governments and the implementing partner, wherever engaged.
